questions.question: A person who knows everything:
questions.explanation: 'Omniscient' means knowing everything.

questions.question: One who is all-powerful:
questions.explanation: 'Omnipotent' means having unlimited or universal power.

questions.question: One who is present everywhere:
questions.explanation: 'Omnipresent' means present everywhere simultaneously.

questions.question: A person who loves mankind and works for their welfare:
questions.explanation: 'Philanthropist' is one who promotes the welfare of others through donation of funds.

questions.question: A person who hates mankind:
questions.explanation: 'Misanthrope' is a person who dislikes humankind and avoids human society.

questions.question: One who hates women:
questions.explanation: 'Misogynist' is a person who hates or is prejudiced against women.

questions.question: One who hates the institution of marriage:
questions.explanation: 'Misogamist' is a person who hates marriage.

questions.question: A person who speaks many languages:
questions.explanation: 'Polyglot' is someone who knows and is able to use several languages.

questions.question: A person who collects stamps:
questions.explanation: 'Philatelist' is a person who collects or studies postage stamps.

questions.question: A person who collects coins:
questions.explanation: 'Numismatist' is a collector or student of coins, tokens, and paper money.

questions.question: A lover of books:
questions.explanation: 'Bibliophile' is a person who loves or collects books.

questions.question: A life history of a person written by himself:
questions.explanation: 'Autobiography' is an account of a person's life written by that person.

questions.question: A life history of a person written by another person:
questions.explanation: 'Biography' is the story of a person's life written by someone else.

questions.question: A person who looks at the bright side of things:
questions.explanation: 'Optimist' is one who tends to be hopeful and confident about the future.

questions.question: A person who looks at the dark side of things:
questions.explanation: 'Pessimist' is a person who tends to see the worst aspect of things.

questions.question: One who does not believe in the existence of God:
questions.explanation: 'Atheist' is a person who disbelieves or lacks belief in the existence of God.

questions.question: One who believes in the existence of God:
questions.explanation: 'Theist' is a person who believes in the existence of a god or gods.

questions.question: One who is not sure about the existence of God:
questions.explanation: 'Agnostic' believes nothing is known or can be known of the existence or nature of God.

questions.question: A person who believes that all events are predetermined by fate:
questions.explanation: 'Fatalist' is one who believes that all events are predetermined and inevitable.

questions.question: A person who is indifferent to pleasure or pain:
questions.explanation: 'Stoic' is a person who can endure pain or hardship without showing feelings or complaining.

questions.question: A person who eats human flesh:
questions.explanation: 'Cannibal' is an animal or human that feeds on flesh of its own species.

questions.question: An animal that eats only plants:
questions.explanation: 'Herbivore' feeds on plants.

questions.question: An animal that feeds on flesh:
questions.explanation: 'Carnivore' feeds on flesh.

questions.question: An animal that feeds on both plants and flesh:
questions.explanation: 'Omnivore' eats food of both plant and animal origin.

questions.question: A medicine that counteracts the effects of poison:
questions.explanation: 'Antidote' neutralizes or counteracts the effects of a poison.

questions.question: A substance that prevents the growth of disease-causing microorganisms:
questions.explanation: 'Antiseptic' prevents the growth of disease-causing microorganisms on living tissue.

questions.question: A medicine that relieves pain:
questions.explanation: 'Analgesic' acts to relieve pain.

questions.question: A medicine that reduces fever:
questions.explanation: 'Antipyretic' reduces fever.

questions.question: Murder of a human being:
questions.explanation: 'Homicide' is the killing of one person by another.

questions.question: Murder of one's father:
questions.explanation: 'Patricide' is the killing of one's father.

questions.question: Murder of one's mother:
questions.explanation: 'Matricide' is the killing of one's mother.

questions.question: Murder of one's brother:
questions.explanation: 'Fratricide' is the killing of one's brother.

questions.question: Murder of one's sister:
questions.explanation: 'Sororicide' is the killing of one's sister.

questions.question: Murder of a king or queen:
questions.explanation: 'Regicide' is the action of killing a king.

questions.question: Murder of one's wife:
questions.explanation: 'Uxoricide' is the killing of one's wife.

questions.question: Killing of a whole race or ethnic group:
questions.explanation: 'Genocide' is the deliberate killing of a large group of people of a particular ethnic group.

questions.question: The act of intentionally killing oneself:
questions.explanation: 'Suicide' is the act of intentionally causing one's own death.

questions.question: Killing of an infant:
questions.explanation: 'Infanticide' is the intentional killing of infants.

questions.question: A person who compiles a dictionary:
questions.explanation: 'Lexicographer' is a person who compiles dictionaries.

questions.question: A person who draws maps:
questions.explanation: 'Cartographer' is a person who draws or produces maps.

questions.question: A person skilled in beautiful handwriting:
questions.explanation: 'Calligrapher' is a person skilled in the art of calligraphy.

questions.question: Bad handwriting:
questions.explanation: 'Cacography' means bad handwriting or incorrect spelling.

questions.question: A speech delivered without any prior preparation:
questions.explanation: 'Extempore' (or impromptu) is spoken or done without preparation.

questions.question: The first public speech delivered by a person:
questions.explanation: 'Maiden speech' is the first speech delivered by a newly elected politician or speaker.

questions.question: A speech praising someone who has died:
questions.explanation: 'Eulogy' is a speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly, typically after death.

questions.question: An inscription on a tombstone:
questions.explanation: 'Epitaph' is a phrase or statement written in memory of a person who has died, especially as on a tombstone.

questions.question: A poem mourning the death of someone:
questions.explanation: 'Elegy' is a poem of serious reflection, typically a lament for the dead.

questions.question: Government by the people, of the people, and for the people:
questions.explanation: 'Democracy' is government by the people.

questions.question: Government by a king or queen:
questions.explanation: 'Monarchy' is a form of government with a monarch at the head.

questions.question: Government by the wealthy:
questions.explanation: 'Plutocracy' is government by the wealthy class.

questions.question: Government by religious leaders or divine guidance:
questions.explanation: 'Theocracy' is a system of government in which priests rule in the name of God.

questions.question: Government by a small privileged group:
questions.explanation: 'Oligarchy' is a small group of people having control of a country.

questions.question: Government by the nobility or privileged upper class:
questions.explanation: 'Aristocracy' is government by the highest social class.

questions.question: Government by state officials and non-elected bureaucrats:
questions.explanation: 'Bureaucracy' is administration characterized by official procedure and hierarchy.

questions.question: A state of disorder due to absence or non-recognition of authority:
questions.explanation: 'Anarchy' is a state of disorder due to absence of government.

questions.question: Government by a single ruler with absolute power:
questions.explanation: 'Autocracy' is a system of government by one person with absolute power.

questions.question: Government by the inexperienced or worst citizens:
questions.explanation: 'Kakistocracy' is government by the least suitable or worst citizens.

questions.question: Government by old people:
questions.explanation: 'Gerontocracy' is a state ruled by elders.

questions.question: A person who has excessive love or admiration for himself:
questions.explanation: 'Narcissist' is a person who has an excessive interest in or admiration of themselves.

questions.question: A person who lives a solitary life and devotes himself to religious discipline:
questions.explanation: 'Ascetic' practices severe self-discipline and abstention from all forms of indulgence.

questions.question: One who believes that pleasure is the most important thing in life:
questions.explanation: 'Hedonist' believes pursuit of pleasure is the primary goal of life.

questions.question: A person who abstains completely from alcoholic drinks:
questions.explanation: 'Teetotaler' is a person who never drinks alcohol.

questions.question: A person who walks in his sleep:
questions.explanation: 'Somnambulist' is a sleepwalker.

questions.question: A person who talks in his sleep:
questions.explanation: 'Somniloquist' is one who talks while asleep.

questions.question: A person who can make his voice appear to come from somewhere else:
questions.explanation: 'Ventriloquist' can speak without moving his lips so that voice appears from elsewhere.

questions.question: A person who cannot be corrected or reformed:
questions.explanation: 'Incorrigible' is not able to be corrected, improved, or reformed.

questions.question: One who makes no mistakes; incapable of making mistakes:
questions.explanation: 'Infallible' means incapable of making mistakes or being wrong.

questions.question: That which cannot be conquered or defeated:
questions.explanation: 'Invincible' means too powerful to be defeated or overcome.

questions.question: That which cannot be wounded or hurt:
questions.explanation: 'Invulnerable' means impossible to harm or damage.

questions.question: A mark that cannot be removed or erased:
questions.explanation: 'Indelible' ink or pen marks cannot be removed.

questions.question: Handwriting that is impossible or difficult to read:
questions.explanation: 'Illegible' means not clear enough to be read.

questions.question: Sound that cannot be heard:
questions.explanation: 'Inaudible' means unable to be heard.

questions.question: A story that is too extraordinary to be believed:
questions.explanation: 'Incredible' means impossible or very difficult to believe.

questions.question: A person who easily believes anything told to him:
questions.explanation: 'Credulous' means showing too great a readiness to believe things; gullible.

questions.question: A person who is qualified and fit to be chosen:
questions.explanation: 'Eligible' means having the right to do or obtain something; satisfying conditions.

questions.question: A disease that is liable to be transmitted to people, organisms, etc. through the environment or contact:
questions.explanation: 'Contagious' disease is spread from one person or organism to another, typically by direct contact.

questions.question: A disease that ends in death:
questions.explanation: 'Fatal' means causing death.

questions.question: A disease that is widespread throughout a region or the world:
questions.explanation: 'Pandemic' is prevalent over an entire country or the world.

questions.question: An epidemic disease found regularly among particular people or in a certain area:
questions.explanation: 'Endemic' is regularly found and very common among a particular group or in a particular area.

questions.question: A place where birds are kept:
questions.explanation: 'Aviary' is a large cage, building, or enclosure for keeping birds in.

questions.question: A place where bees are kept:
questions.explanation: 'Apiary' is a place where bees are kept; a collection of beehives.

questions.question: A place where fish and water animals are kept:
questions.explanation: 'Aquarium' is a transparent tank in which fish and other water creatures are kept.

questions.question: A place where animals are slaughtered for food:
questions.explanation: 'Abattoir' is a slaughterhouse.

questions.question: A place where dead human bodies are kept before burial or cremation:
questions.explanation: 'Mortuary' is a room or building in which dead bodies are kept.

questions.question: A place where bodies are kept for identification and autopsy:
questions.explanation: 'Morgue' is a place where bodies of deceased persons are kept for identification.

questions.question: A burial ground where dead bodies are buried:
questions.explanation: 'Cemetery' is a large burial ground.

questions.question: A place where dead bodies are cremated:
questions.explanation: 'Crematorium' is a place where a dead person's body is cremated.

questions.question: A place where weapons and ammunition are stored:
questions.explanation: 'Arsenal' is a collection of weapons and military equipment or the place where they are stored.

questions.question: A place where grain is stored:
questions.explanation: 'Granary' is a storehouse for threshed grain.

questions.question: A building where government or historical records are preserved:
questions.explanation: 'Archives' is a collection of historical documents or records.

questions.question: A collection of wild animals kept in captivity for exhibition:
questions.explanation: 'Menagerie' is a collection of wild animals kept in captivity for exhibition.

questions.question: A medicine that induces sleep:
questions.explanation: 'Soporific' tends to induce drowsiness or sleep.

questions.question: Inability to sleep:
questions.explanation: 'Insomnia' is habitual sleeplessness; inability to sleep.

questions.question: Partial or total loss of memory:
questions.explanation: 'Amnesia' is a partial or total loss of memory.

questions.question: Loss of ability to feel pain while still conscious:
questions.explanation: 'Analgesia' is the inability to feel pain.

questions.question: Loss of ability to understand or express speech:
questions.explanation: 'Aphasia' is loss of ability to understand or express speech, caused by brain damage.

questions.question: A cure for all diseases; a universal remedy:
questions.explanation: 'Panacea' is a solution or remedy for all difficulties or diseases.

questions.question: A person who leaves his own country to settle permanently in another:
questions.explanation: 'Emigrant' leaves their country (exit); 'Immigrant' enters a new country (in).

questions.question: A person who comes to live permanently in a foreign country:
questions.explanation: 'Immigrant' comes to live permanently in a foreign country.

questions.question: A person without a home or job who moves from place to place:
questions.explanation: 'Vagrant' wanders from place to place without a home or job.

questions.question: A person who has unusual or eccentric habits:
questions.explanation: 'Eccentric' is a person of unconventional and slightly strange views or behavior.

questions.question: A socially unconventional person, especially an artist or writer:
questions.explanation: 'Bohemian' is an unconventional person living an artistic lifestyle.

questions.question: A person who is indifferent or hostile to culture, arts, and intellect:
questions.explanation: 'Philistine' is a person who is hostile or indifferent to culture and the arts.

questions.question: A person who deliberately damages or destroys public property:
questions.explanation: 'Vandal' deliberately destroys or damages public or private property.

questions.question: A decision on which all members agree completely:
questions.explanation: 'Unanimous' means held or arrived at by the agreement of all members.

questions.question: One who looks at the bright side of things:
questions.explanation: An optimist always looks at the positive side.

questions.question: One who looks at the dark side of things:
questions.explanation: A pessimist expects the worst.

questions.question: A person who believes that all events are predetermined by fate:
questions.explanation: A fatalist believes fate governs everything.

questions.question: One who does not believe in the existence of God:
questions.explanation: An atheist rejects belief in deities.

questions.question: One who is doubtful about the existence of God:
questions.explanation: An agnostic claims the existence of God is unknowable.

questions.question: One who loves and collects books:
questions.explanation: 'Bibliophile' is a lover and collector of books.

questions.question: One who collects postage stamps:
questions.explanation: A 'Philatelist' studies and collects stamps.

questions.question: One who collects coins and medals:
questions.explanation: A 'Numismatist' collects and studies currency and medals.

questions.question: One who draws or produces maps:
questions.explanation: A 'Cartographer' makes geographical maps.

questions.question: One who writes beautiful handwriting:
questions.explanation: A 'Calligrapher' specializes in artistic script.

questions.question: A person who hates women:
questions.explanation: 'Misogynist' is one who harbors hatred towards women.

questions.question: A person who hates marriage:
questions.explanation: 'Misogamist' hates the institution of marriage.

questions.question: A person who hates mankind:
questions.explanation: 'Misanthrope' dislikes humankind and society.

questions.question: A lover of mankind who works for human welfare:
questions.explanation: 'Philanthropist' devotes wealth and care to human welfare.

questions.question: A person who eats human flesh:
questions.explanation: A 'Cannibal' consumes the flesh of its own species.

questions.question: An animal that feeds on plants:
questions.explanation: 'Herbivore' feeds strictly on vegetation.

questions.question: An animal that eats both plants and meat:
questions.explanation: 'Omnivore' consumes both animal and plant matter.

questions.question: One who is indifferent to pain or pleasure:
questions.explanation: A 'Stoic' endures hardship without complaint.

questions.question: One who lives for pleasure and sensory enjoyment:
questions.explanation: 'Hedonist' believes pursuit of pleasure is the primary good.

questions.question: A person who practices severe self-discipline and avoids all indulgence:
questions.explanation: An 'Ascetic' renounces worldly pleasures for spiritual goals.

questions.question: A remedy for all diseases or difficulties:
questions.explanation: 'Panacea' is a universal cure-all.

questions.question: A medicine that counteracts the effects of poison:
questions.explanation: 'Antidote' neutralizes toxins.

questions.question: Murder of a king or queen:
questions.explanation: 'Regicide' is the assassination of a monarch.

questions.question: Murder of one's father:
questions.explanation: 'Patricide' is the killing of one's father.

questions.question: Murder of one's mother:
questions.explanation: 'Matricide' is the murder of one's mother.

questions.question: Murder of one's brother:
questions.explanation: 'Fratricide' is the killing of a brother.

questions.question: Murder of an infant or newborn baby:
questions.explanation: 'Infanticide' is the killing of an infant.

questions.question: Deliberate killing of a large group of people from a particular nation or ethnic group:
questions.explanation: 'Genocide' is the systemic extermination of a people.

questions.question: A post or office with high salary but no work:
questions.explanation: 'Sinecure' is a remunerative position requiring little or no responsibility.

questions.question: A position held without remuneration or salary:
questions.explanation: 'Honorary' work is done without payment.

questions.question: A government ruled by a single person with absolute power:
questions.explanation: 'Autocracy' is rule by one individual with supreme power.

questions.question: A government by the wealthy class:
questions.explanation: 'Plutocracy' is governance by the rich.

questions.question: A government ruled by religious leaders or priests:
questions.explanation: 'Theocracy' is rule by clerics under divine authority.

questions.question: A government ruled by a small group of powerful individuals:
questions.explanation: 'Oligarchy' is political power concentrated in a few individuals.

questions.question: A state of disorder due to the absence of government or authority:
questions.explanation: 'Anarchy' is lawlessness from lack of government.

questions.question: One who speaks many languages fluently:
questions.explanation: A 'Polyglot' speaks multiple languages.

questions.question: The first public speech delivered by an orator:
questions.explanation: 'Maiden speech' is a speaker's inaugural parliamentary or formal address.

questions.question: A speech made without any prior preparation:
questions.explanation: 'Extempore' or 'Impromptu' is spoken offhand without advance preparation.

questions.question: A poem or song lamenting the death of someone:
questions.explanation: An 'Elegy' is a mournful funeral poem.

questions.question: A life story written by oneself:
questions.explanation: 'Autobiography' is self-written life history.

questions.question: A life story written by another person:
questions.explanation: 'Biography' is another person's account of a life.

questions.question: A place where birds are kept:
questions.explanation: 'Aviary' is an enclosure for confining birds (cf. 'Apiary' for bees).

questions.question: A place where bees are kept:
questions.explanation: 'Apiary' is a bee yard or collection of beehives.

questions.question: A place where weapons and ammunition are stored:
questions.explanation: An 'Arsenal' is a storehouse for arms.

questions.question: A doctor who specializes in skin diseases:
questions.explanation: 'Dermatologist' specializes in treating skin disorders.

questions.question: A doctor who specializes in heart ailments:
questions.explanation: 'Cardiologist' specializes in the cardiovascular system.

questions.question: A doctor who treats children:
questions.explanation: 'Pediatrician' treats children and their diseases.

questions.question: A doctor who specializes in eye disorders:
questions.explanation: 'Ophthalmologist' specializes in ocular medicine.

questions.question: A person who walks in sleep:
questions.explanation: 'Somnambulist' is a sleepwalker.

questions.question: A person who talks in sleep:
questions.explanation: 'Somniloquist' talks while sleeping.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'A secret or disguised way of writing'
questions.explanation: 'Cypher': A cypher or cipher is a secret code or cryptographic system.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'The therapeutic use of sunlight for healing'
questions.explanation: 'Heliotherapy': Heliotherapy uses sunlight exposure for medical treatments.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'One who studies elections and voting statistics'
questions.explanation: 'Psephologist': A psephologist analyzes voting trends and election data.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'Government according to fixed rule of law'
questions.explanation: 'Nomocracy': Nomocracy is a political system governed by supreme rule of law.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'Safe and suitable for drinking'
questions.explanation: 'Potable': Potable water is fit for human consumption.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'Using the exact same words as originally spoken or written'
questions.explanation: 'Verbatim': Verbatim means word-for-word replication.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'The emblems, insignia, or dress of royalty'
questions.explanation: 'Regalia': Regalia refers to royal crowns, scepters, and official coronation items.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'An imaginary ideal society where everything is perfect'
questions.explanation: 'Utopia': Utopia (from Thomas More) is a visionary perfect society.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'A thing kept as a reminder of a place, person, or event'
questions.explanation: 'Souvenir': A souvenir or memento is preserved as a memory.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'A fortress commanding a city and serving as last retreat'
questions.explanation: 'Citadel': A citadel is a fortified stronghold on elevated ground.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'An inescapable agent of someone's downfall or deserved punishment'
questions.explanation: 'Nemesis': Nemesis (Greek goddess of retribution) denotes fatal downfall.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'Something absolutely necessary that cannot be done without'
questions.explanation: 'Indispensable': Indispensable means essential and incapable of replacement.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'The act of copying another author's language and claiming it as one's own'
questions.explanation: 'Plagiarism': Plagiarism is academic theft of intellectual material.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'A person who cuts, polishes, or engraves precious gemstones'
questions.explanation: 'Lapidary': A lapidary is a skilled craftsperson working with gems.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'A person made to bear blame or suffer for the sins of others'
questions.explanation: 'Scapegoat': A scapegoat is made to carry collective guilt.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'Disposed to believe too readily without proof / gullible'
questions.explanation: 'Credulous': A credulous person is easily deceived due to over-trusting nature.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'Deliberate destruction or damage to impede an enemy or employer'
questions.explanation: 'Sabotage': Sabotage involves subversive destruction of infrastructure.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'A closed meeting of political party members to choose candidates'
questions.explanation: 'Caucus': A caucus is an inner conference of party delegates.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'The legal right to vote in public political elections'
questions.explanation: 'Suffrage': Suffrage denotes the franchise or political voting rights.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'A person who advocates for the social and political equality of all people'
questions.explanation: 'Egalitarian': Egalitarianism champions universal human equality.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'One who opposes war and believes all violence is unjustifiable'
questions.explanation: 'Pacifist': A pacifist rejects armed conflict and military aggression.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'The medieval forerunner of chemistry aimed at transmuting metals'
questions.explanation: 'Alchemy': Alchemy sought the philosopher's stone to transmute lead into gold.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'A man who has womanish habits, speech, or gestures'
questions.explanation: 'Effeminate': Effeminate denotes unmanly traits in male behavior.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'A book, document, or piece of music written by hand'
questions.explanation: 'Manuscript': A manuscript (manu + scriptum) is handwritten text.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'A large building or shed designed for housing aircraft'
questions.explanation: 'Hangar': An aircraft hangar provides sheltered storage for airplanes.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'The act of speaking irreverently or disrespectfully about God or sacred things'
questions.explanation: 'Blasphemy': Blasphemy is profanity or sacrilege towards sacred matters.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'The statistical study of human population and vital records'
questions.explanation: 'Demography': Demography charts population trends, birth rates, and migration.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'Possessing unlimited, absolute, and supreme power'
questions.explanation: 'Omnipotent': Omnipotent (all-powerful) is an attribute ascribed to God.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'The scientific study or collection of coins, medals, and paper money'
questions.explanation: 'Numismatics': Numismatics is the numismatic study of historic currency.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'A small, exclusive clique of persons who associate closely'
questions.explanation: 'Clique': A clique excludes outsiders from its inner circle.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'A repository where historical records and public documents are preserved'
questions.explanation: 'Archive': An archive stores archival historical state records.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'The branch of medicine concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of skin diseases'
questions.explanation: 'Dermatology': Dermatology treats skin, hair, and nail disorders.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'The killing of dogs'
questions.explanation: 'Canicide': Canicide denotes the act of destroying dogs.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'The killing of wolves'
questions.explanation: 'Lupicide': Lupicide denotes the killing of wolves.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'The killing of bears'
questions.explanation: 'Ursicide': Ursicide denotes the destruction of bears.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'An irrational and intense fear of enclosed or confined spaces'
questions.explanation: 'Claustrophobia': Claustrophobia is panic triggered by enclosed spaces.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'Intense dislike of or prejudice against people from other countries'
questions.explanation: 'Xenophobia': Xenophobia is fear or hatred of foreigners.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'An irrational and morbid fear of dogs'
questions.explanation: 'Cynophobia': Cynophobia is clinical phobia of dogs.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'An extreme or irrational fear of heights'
questions.explanation: 'Acrophobia': Acrophobia causes vertigo and terror at elevated altitudes.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'An obsessive impulse to set fire to buildings or objects'
questions.explanation: 'Pyromania': Pyromania is pathological fire-starting.

questions.question: Give one word for: 'A recurrent, uncontrollable urge to steal items without economic motive'
questions.explanation: 'Kleptomania': Kleptomania is compulsive stealing.
